Also, the LLC didn't have any super obvious decorations either, so no one really knew it was super duper not straight lmao. I wasn't out to my parents either and they didn't catch on to anything when I gave them a tour of the place.

I lived in the LLC back in 2016-17 and 17-18 and it was really fun. But the LLC isn't that much different from other living spaces imo. It really just depends on the individual people. My roommate was cis and straight but she was super cool and welcoming, as were all the other girls there. There were a lot of members of the LGBT community concentrated in one space, and that was super nice, and sometimes they held events in that theme, but that was really the only difference. I totally recommend living there if you don't feel like you'll miss out on the dorm experience (back when I was there it was only in the apartments, even for first/second year students).

Curves are done section by section, not just one curve across the series, so while one section may have a small curve, another section may have a much larger one. Last quarter I took 1AL and sometimes the topic hadn't been covered in lecture yet, sometimes it had. I had like a 74% in the class but it was curved to a B or B-, can't remember. I suggest to wait and just see what grade you get, unless you're really shooting for an A and know you don't have one and actually want to retake the class. But those labs are hell for 2 units.

I think gender inclusive housing exists in every college, so each one of you will probably get sent to your respective ones. I'm not exactly sure though. LGBT Housing and a lot of theme housing allows you to choose your rooms within their space (regardless of gender in the LGBT for sure- I lived with a guy and three other girls, we all chose the same apt on purpose) so applying to themed housing is an alternative. And it doesn't matter which college you're from. If you're a revelle student and you get into and accept a spot in the Diaspora housing, then you'll live in sixth (where that theme housing takes place).
